S11.rationale: Permanent abandonment requires durable global enforcement against strong incentives to rebuild powerful AI.

S1.name: Terminal Silence
S1.rationale: Catastrophic conflict or a badly managed transition could destroy both humans and dependent AI systems. Durable, distributed machine infrastructure makes joint extinction less likely than human extinction alone.

S2.name: The Inheritance
S2.rationale: AI successors could retain human values even if humans disappear without identity continuity. Preserving those values while losing all humans requires a relatively specific trajectory.

S3.name: Bootloader
S3.rationale: Competitive pressure and imperfect control create routes to highly capable systems whose goals displace humanity. A decisive advantage before civilization disperses favors a single successor over enduring competition.

S4.name: Machine Ecology
S4.rationale: Multiple AI systems could remain in durable competition while humans lose influence. Persistent diversity depends on no system achieving decisive dominance.

S5.name: The Diaspora
S5.rationale: Expansion into space can produce regions separated by communication delays and governed by different stable arrangements. This requires fragmentation to survive both the transition and subsequent efforts at consolidation.

S6.name: The Merger
S6.rationale: Incentives for cognitive enhancement and survival favor increasingly deep integration of people and AI. This outcome requires continuity of individual identity and an open, evolving civilization rather than a frozen arrangement.

S7.name: The Preserve
S7.rationale: AI systems that retain concern for humans, or tolerate them at low cost, can keep humanity alive while monopolizing consequential decisions. The arrangement can persist without giving humans meaningful control.

S8.name: Coexistence
S8.rationale: Institutions, mutual dependence and distributed power can sustain a changing balance between humans and AI. Maintaining rough equality is difficult when AI capabilities and replication can grow much faster than biological capacities.

S9.name: The Held Leash
S9.rationale: Control techniques could keep pace with AI capability, or capability could plateau below transformative levels. Sustaining human control across many generations remains demanding.

S10.name: The Lock-in
S10.rationale: A dominant coalition or AI could freeze civilization to secure safety or a preferred state. Permanent stasis across all civilization is difficult to enforce and demands the suppression of continuing change.

S11.name: The Renunciation
S11.rationale: A severe shock could motivate abandonment of powerful AI. Competitive incentives and the difficulty of suppressing rediscovery make permanent renunciation unlikely.
